n0001.title: Moby Dick; or The Whale
n0001.gist: Ishmael narrates the Pequod's fated voyage as Captain Ahab drives his crew across the world's oceans in a monomaniacal hunt for the white whale that maimed him, a chase that ultimately destroys the ship and all but one man.

n0002.title: Front Matter and Etymology
n0002.gist: The novel opens with publication notices, a table of contents, and transcriber's notes before the narrative proper begins.

n0003.title: Title and Publication Notices
n0003.gist: The book is announced with its title, author byline, and Project Gutenberg framing.

n0009.title: Contents
n0009.gist: A full chapter listing previews the entire voyage the novel will narrate.

n0011.title: Original Transcriber's Notes
n0011.gist: The editors explain the textual sources used to assemble this etext edition.

n0015.title: Ishmael Goes to Sea
n0015.gist: Ishmael explains his restless urge to sail, travels to New Bedford, and forges an unlikely bond with the cannibal harpooneer Queequeg before they head to Nantucket to sign aboard a whaler.

n0016.title: Loomings
n0016.gist: Ishmael declares that whenever he grows grim ashore he takes to the sea as his cure for melancholy.

n0033.title: Finding Lodging in New Bedford
n0033.gist: Arriving too late for the Nantucket packet, Ishmael wanders cold New Bedford streets seeking cheap lodging and stumbles into the ominous Spouter-Inn.

n0047.title: Meeting Queequeg
n0047.gist: At the Spouter-Inn, Ishmael reluctantly agrees to share a bed with the tattooed cannibal harpooneer Queequeg and, after a terrifying introduction, comes to trust and befriend him.

n0123.title: Waking Beside Queequeg
n0123.gist: Ishmael wakes tangled in Queequeg's embrace and reflects on the strangeness of the sensation before the two rise and dress for the day.

n0132.title: Breakfast and the Street
n0132.gist: Ishmael observes the rough camaraderie of whalemen at breakfast and then tours New Bedford's streets, marveling at its wealth built entirely on whale oil.

n0153.title: The Whaleman's Chapel
n0153.gist: Ishmael visits the Whaleman's Chapel, reads memorial tablets to sailors lost at sea, and hears Father Mapple deliver a thunderous sermon on Jonah's disobedience and repentance.

n0197.title: Bonding with Queequeg
n0197.gist: Back at the inn, Ishmael grows genuinely fond of Queequeg, learns his life story as an island prince who fled home to see Christendom, and agrees to sail with him to Nantucket.

n0223.title: Voyage to Nantucket
n0223.gist: Ishmael and Queequeg travel by wheelbarrow and schooner to Nantucket, where Queequeg heroically saves a drowning man, cementing his quiet nobility before they reach the whaling island itself.

n0240.title: Nantucket and the Try Pots
n0240.gist: Ishmael praises Nantucket as the whaling world's capital and the pair lodge at the chowder-serving Try Pots inn while preparing to find a ship.

n0265.title: Signing Aboard the Pequod
n0265.gist: Ishmael and Queequeg choose and sign onto the whaling ship Pequod under its eccentric Quaker owners, learn the crew is bound to a mysterious absent captain, and are shadowed by the cryptic beggar-prophet Elijah before departure.

n0266.title: Choosing the Pequod
n0266.gist: Guided by Queequeg's idol Yojo, Ishmael selects the ornately whalebone-decorated Pequod and negotiates a modest lay with the blustering owners Peleg and Bildad.

n0349.title: Ramadan and Queequeg's Fasting
n0349.gist: While Queequeg observes a daylong religious fast that alarms the crew, Ishmael muses on tolerance for others' beliefs and gently argues Queequeg out of excessive austerity.

n0381.title: Queequeg Signs On
n0381.gist: Despite the owners' religious suspicions, Queequeg dazzles Peleg and Bildad with his harpooning skill and signs the ship's articles with his mark.

n0407.title: Elijah's Warnings
n0407.gist: A ragged stranger named Elijah accosts Ishmael and Queequeg with cryptic, ominous warnings about Captain Ahab and the Pequod's fate.

n0447.title: Preparations and Elijah's Return
n0447.gist: The ship is provisioned for departure while Elijah reappears at the dock with unsettling hints, and the crew boards amid an atmosphere of foreboding.

n0449.title: Departure and the Hidden Captain
n0449.gist: The Pequod sets sail under the visible command of Peleg and Bildad while the true captain, Ahab, remains mysteriously confined below, and Ishmael reflects on the peril and moral standing of the whaling trade.

n0450.title: Going Aboard
n0450.gist: Ishmael and Queequeg board the readying Pequod before dawn and encounter a sleeping rigger who confirms Ahab came aboard the previous night.

n0498.title: Setting Sail on Christmas
n0498.gist: On a cold Christmas Day the Pequod casts off under Peleg and Bildad's blustering command, with Ahab still unseen belowdecks as the ship heads to open sea.

n0522.title: The Lee Shore and Bulkington
n0522.gist: Ishmael eulogizes the sailor Bulkington, using his refusal of safe harbor as a symbol of the soul's need to seek truth over comfort.

n0528.title: In Defense of Whaling
n0528.gist: Ishmael mounts a spirited defense of whaling's dignity and historical importance against landsmen's scorn, citing its economic and cultural impact.

n0553.title: Postscript on Sperm Oil
n0553.gist: Ishmael adds a wry note suggesting royal coronation oils are likely derived from prized sperm whale oil.

n0560.title: The Officers and Crew
n0560.gist: Ishmael profiles the Pequod's mates, harpooneers, and enigmatic Captain Ahab, revealing the ship's diverse, fated crew and the hidden mysticism of Ahab's obsessive quest before it is fully declared.

n0561.title: Starbuck and Stubb
n0561.gist: Ishmael introduces the pious, prudent chief mate Starbuck and the easygoing, pipe-smoking second mate Stubb, contrasting their temperaments.

n0568.title: Flask and the Harpooneers
n0568.gist: Ishmael describes the pugnacious third mate Flask alongside the three pagan harpooneers Queequeg, Tashtego, and Daggoo who serve the mates.

n0579.title: Ahab Appears
n0579.gist: After days hidden below, the scarred, ivory-legged Captain Ahab finally appears on deck, radiating a grim, commanding, and troubled majesty.

n0588.title: Ahab Clashes with Stubb
n0588.gist: Ahab's foul mood erupts when he harshly rebukes Stubb for a minor complaint, leaving Stubb bewildered and uneasy about the captain's volatile nature.
n0588.sourceHeading: CHAPTER 29. Enter Ahab; to Him, Stubb.

n0601.title: Ahab's Vow and Cetology
n0601.gist: Ahab dramatically reveals his true purpose of hunting Moby Dick and binds the crew to his vengeance with a fiery oath, while Ishmael pauses to catalog whale species and set the scientific stage for the hunt.

n0602.title: The Pipe and Queen Mab
n0602.gist: Ahab broods alone over his pipe before casting it into the sea, while Stubb recounts a strange dream about Ahab's ivory leg to Flask.

n0615.title: The Quarter-Deck Oath
n0615.gist: Ahab nails a gold doubloon to the mast and, in a fevered speech, compels the crew to swear vengeance against Moby Dick, overriding Starbuck's moral objections.

n0663.title: Sunset, Dusk, and Night Soliloquies
n0663.gist: In successive private monologues, Ahab, Starbuck, and Stubb each reveal their conflicted inner responses to the oath and the voyage's dark trajectory.

n0665.title: First Whale Chases
n0665.gist: The Pequod's crew undertakes its first dangerous whale hunts and processing work, while Ahab's mysterious extra boat crew led by Fedallah is revealed and eerie omens accumulate around the ship.

n0666.title: The Specksnyder and Cabin Hierarchy
n0666.gist: Ishmael explains the historical role of the harpooneer-officer and describes the rigid social hierarchy governing meals in Ahab's cabin.

n0674.title: First Lowering and Ahab's Secret Crew
n0674.gist: A whale sighting prompts a chaotic first lowering of the boats, revealing that Ahab has secretly smuggled aboard his own boat crew led by the Parsee Fedallah.

n0676.title: Whale Anatomy and Whaling Lore
n0676.gist: Ishmael digresses extensively into the anatomy, historical depictions, and philosophical significance of whales, interspersed with encounters with other ships that deepen the sense of Moby Dick's legendary danger.

n0677.title: The Whale's Head and Whiteness
n0677.gist: Ishmael examines the sperm and right whale's contrasting heads in detail, then meditates at length on why the whale's whiteness inspires such profound terror.

n1060.title: The Town-Ho's Story
n1060.gist: Ishmael recounts, as a tale told to Peruvian friends, the story of the ship Town-Ho where a mutinous sailor's vengeance was fulfilled indirectly by Moby Dick himself.

n1174.title: Pictures and Cultural Images of Whales
n1174.gist: Ishmael surveys inaccurate artistic and scientific depictions of whales throughout history, arguing the living leviathan resists true representation.
n1174.sourceHeading: CHAPTER 55. Of the Monstrous Pictures of Whales.

n1211.title: Squid, Brit, and Sea Life
n1211.gist: The Pequod encounters an ominous giant squid and fields of brit, prompting Ishmael's reflections on the ocean's simultaneous beauty and menace.

n1239.title: The Whale-Line and Its Perils
n1239.gist: Ishmael explains the coiled whale-line's deadly mechanics aboard the boats, framing it as a symbol of the ever-present peril surrounding human life.

n1560.title: Encountering the Jungfrau and Bachelor
n1560.gist: The Pequod meets several other whaling ships including the oil-starved Jungfrau and the jubilant, fully-laden Bachelor, contrasting their fortunes with Ahab's grim quest.
n1560.sourceHeading: CHAPTER 81. The Pequod Meets The Virgin.

n1894.title: The Samuel Enderby and the Lost Arm
n1894.gist: The Pequod meets the English ship Samuel Enderby, whose captain lost an arm to Moby Dick and wisely refuses further pursuit, foiling Ahab's urgent questioning.

n1953.title: Whale Skeleton and Fossil History
n1953.gist: Ishmael examines a whale skeleton preserved in a Pacific island temple and argues from fossil evidence that whales are ancient, immortal as a species, and unlikely to face extinction.
n1953.sourceHeading: CHAPTER 102. A Bower in the Arsacides.

n2009.title: Ahab's Deepening Obsession
n2009.gist: As the Pequod nears its quarry, Ahab's monomania intensifies through symbolic acts—forging a special harpoon, defying his officers, and destroying his own instruments—while ambiguous omens multiply around the ship.

n2010.title: Ahab's New Leg and Wound
n2010.gist: After his ivory leg is damaged, Ahab has the carpenter fashion a replacement, prompting Ahab's brooding meditation on suffering, fate, and mortality.

n2018.title: The Carpenter and Ahab's Musings
n2018.gist: Ishmael profiles the ship's stolid, all-purpose carpenter before Ahab engages him in an eerie philosophical exchange about pain, identity, and mortality.

n2064.title: Conflict Over the Leaking Oil
n2064.gist: Starbuck confronts Ahab about a serious oil leak threatening the voyage's profit, but Ahab nearly threatens him at gunpoint before relenting to fix the casks.
n2064.sourceHeading: CHAPTER 109. Ahab and Starbuck in the Cabin.

n2088.title: Queequeg's Near-Death and Coffin
n2088.gist: Queequeg falls gravely ill and has a coffin built to his specifications, then inexplicably recovers and repurposes the coffin as a sea-chest.

n2112.title: Forging the Special Harpoon
n2112.gist: Ahab has the blacksmith Perth forge a special harpoon tempered with the harpooneers' blood, baptizing it in the devil's name for his final assault on Moby Dick.

n2210.title: The Typhoon and St. Elmo's Fire
n2210.gist: A violent typhoon strikes the ship, corpusant flames burn on the masts, and Ahab defiantly worships the fire while extinguishing his own harpoon's flame before the crew.

n2267.title: Starbuck's Temptation
n2267.gist: Alone with a loaded musket outside Ahab's door, Starbuck agonizes over whether to kill his captain to save the ship, but ultimately cannot bring himself to act.

n2282.title: Compass and Log Line Failures
n2282.gist: The typhoon reverses the ship's compass needles and severs the log line, and Ahab defiantly re-magnetizes a needle himself to reassert control over fate.

n2355.title: The Life-Buoy and Pip's Descent
n2355.gist: A sailor drowns retrieving the ship's rotted life-buoy, so Queequeg's coffin is repurposed as a new one, while the traumatized cabin boy Pip, driven mad after being abandoned at sea, becomes Ahab's strange companion.

n2381.title: The Final Chase
n2381.gist: The Pequod encounters the grief-stricken Rachel searching for lost sailors, and Ahab, deaf to Starbuck's pleas and his own softened humanity, drives the ship into a climactic three-day chase that destroys the Pequod and all aboard save Ishmael.

n2382.title: The Rachel's Lost Son
n2382.gist: Captain Gardiner of the Rachel begs Ahab to help search for his missing son's boat crew, but Ahab coldly refuses and sails on toward his own quarry.

n2402.title: Ahab's Human Moment
n2402.gist: In a rare tender scene, Ahab confides in Starbuck about his lonely life and family, briefly seeming to waver before hardening again toward his fatal purpose.

n2463.title: First Day of the Chase
n2463.gist: Moby Dick is finally sighted and the first day's chase ends in a stove boat and Ahab nearly drowned, but he emerges more fiercely resolved than ever.

n2516.title: Second Day of the Chase
n2516.gist: The second day's pursuit destroys more boats and reveals Fedallah's death lashed to the whale, fulfilling part of his prophecy to Ahab.

n2565.title: Third Day and the Ship's Destruction
n2565.gist: On the third day Moby Dick rams and sinks the Pequod itself, Ahab is dragged to his death by his own harpoon line, and the ship vanishes into the sea with all hands.

n2629.title: Epilogue
n2629.gist: Ishmael reveals he alone survived, kept afloat by Queequeg's coffin-turned-life-buoy until the Rachel, still searching for her lost children, rescues him.
